title: A mutual perpetual chase entered by a quiet White move is still a draw

boundary.expect: second occurrence; not yet a draw by mutual violation

rationale: The mx-mix-002 wheel reached by a quiet entry move instead of beginning at its first occurrence. White's king steps e2e1, which captures nothing, gives no check, and leaves both attack configurations exactly as they stood — the black cannon on b5 is attacked from e5 before and after it, the white cannon on f3 from f7 — so the entry renews no chase; the repeating position then stands on the board at plies 1, 5 and 9. Strictly inside that window each of Black's four moves shuttles the horse between e3 and f5 and switches the attacker on the unprotected white cannon f3 between f7 and c3, and each of White's four moves shuttles the horse between b3 and c5 and switches the attacker on the unprotected black cannon b5 between e5 and b1, so every move of both sides attacks one and the same target from a square it was not attacked from before that move, which is the accepted renewal test; neither target is ever defended and neither side ever gives check. Both sides therefore commit perpetual chase and the mutual rule makes this a draw carrying the reserved reason mutual-perpetual-chase, and the entry move, which lies outside the three-occurrence window, cannot make it anything else. Patch-gated against fork correction P3: the current unpatched engine also intersects the chase set of the quiet entry move, which empties the last mover's accumulator, and returns a unilateral loss for Black — the side that did not enter — so this fixture states the contract against the engine and is expected to fail until that correction lands. Its reason identifier is separately gated on the fork accessor exposing which repetition branch fired, exactly as for mx-mix-002. Review with mx-mix-007, the same wheel entered by Black, whose loser under the unpatched engine is Red instead.
